rules.reason: {model} ignores the top-level effortLevel in {file}. Opus 5.5 and later models take a user settings level only from modelSettings.

quotes.quote: Opus 5.5 and models released after it ignore it and start at their own default until you save a level for them, which `/effort` writes under `modelSettings`. In project, local, and managed settings, and with `--settings`, this key applies to every model.
If you set `effortLevel` in managed settings, Claude Code applies it at the settings step of the effort resolution order, and users can still change the level with `/effort` or `--effort`.

rules.reason: {winner} sets the model. --model beats ANTHROPIC_MODEL, which beats the model key in any file, managed included.

quotes.quote: `--model` takes precedence over `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, and both take precedence over this key for one session, including over a managed `model`

rules.reason: {key} comes from {file}. A settings env block overwrites the shell, and the higher file wins.

quotes.quote: A value here overwrites the same variable exported in your shell, and when more than one settings file sets a variable, the highest-precedence one applies.

rules.reason: {winner} sets the effort. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL beats --effort, which beats every settings file.

quotes.quote: `--effort` takes precedence over this key for one session, and `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` takes precedence over both
If you set `effortLevel` in managed settings, Claude Code applies it at the settings step of the effort resolution order, and users can still change the level with `/effort` or `--effort`.

rules.reason: {file} decides effort for {model}, because it's the highest file that sets a level for this model.

quotes.quote: Across files, Claude Code resolves each model separately: the highest-precedence settings file that sets either an `effortLevel` for that model or a top-level `effortLevel` that applies to that model decides, so an `effortLevel` in managed settings outranks a level you saved in user settings.

rules.reason: The lowest cap applies. {value} in {file} can't be raised from another file.

quotes.quote: When several scopes set a cap, the lowest applies, so a cap set in one scope can't be raised from another

rules.reason: {winner} sets the main conversation's cache lifetime. ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H counts only when no file sets the key.

quotes.quote: `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` takes precedence over everything else, then `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, then this key, and last `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`

rules.reason: {winner} sets the cache lifetime for {agent}. ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H counts only when no file sets the key.

quotes.quote: `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` takes precedence over everything else, then `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, then this key, then `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`, which asks for the one-hour lifetime on every request.

rules.reason: {winner} sets the auto-compact window. CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW beats --autocompact, and both beat managed settings.

quotes.quote: `--autocompact` takes precedence over this key for one session, and `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` takes precedence over both unless Claude Code ignores the variable's value

rules.reason: {agent} runs on {winner}. Its frontmatter model, inherit included, beats CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, which beats the main model. A model passed at dispatch, or set by a mod's agent.spawn hook, beats all three, and the resolver can't see either.

quotes.quote: Two sources take precedence over it: a model Claude passes when it spawns the agent, and a `model` field in the agent's definition, including `inherit`.

rules.reason: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE is on, so {agent} ignores the model in {file} and runs on {winner}.

quotes.quote: While `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` is on, Claude Code ignores the `model` field in subagent definitions, and Claude can't pass a model when it starts a subagent.

rules.reason: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is {value}, so Claude Code sends no effort level and the API's own default for {model} applies. /effort status shows this as auto.

quotes.quote: Set it to `auto` or `unset` to have Claude Code send no effort level, so that the API applies its own default for the model.

rules.reason: Nothing sets an effort level that counts for {model}, so it runs at its default, {value}. /effort status shows this as auto (currently {value}).

quotes.quote: The model's default effort: `high` on every model that supports effort, except that Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 default to `medium`, Opus 4.7 defaults to `xhigh`

rules.reason: {value} isn't a level effortLevel accepts in {file}, so Claude Code skips it and the next source decides. Settings files take low, medium, high or xhigh.

quotes.quote: `max` isn't accepted as a level in either key

rules.reason: {value} isn't a level a modelSettings entry accepts in {file}, so Claude Code skips it for {model} and the next source decides. An entry takes low, medium, high or xhigh.

quotes.quote: `effortLevel`: one of `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or `"xhigh"`

rules.reason: --effort {value} isn't a level Claude Code knows, so it warns and ignores the flag. The next source decides. The docs also list ultracode as a level, but it wasn't tested on 2.1.302, so this rule doesn't treat it as valid.

quotes.quote: Options: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or `ultracode`.

rules.reason: {value} from {file} runs as {becomes}, because maxEffortLevel caps {model} at {becomes}.

quotes.quote: Any higher level runs at the cap instead, including one from `/effort`, the `/model` picker, `--effort`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, a skill's or subagent's `effort` frontmatter, or the model's own default.

rules.reason: {model} has no {value} level, so {value} from {file} runs as {becomes}, the highest level it has below that.

quotes.quote: If you set a level the active model does not support, Claude Code falls back to the highest supported level at or below the one you set. For example, `xhigh` runs as `high` on Opus 4.6.

rules.reason: {model} doesn't support effort, so Claude Code sends no level and {value} from {file} has no effect.

quotes.quote: The available effort levels depend on the model. Models not listed here do not support effort

rules.reason: {agent} runs at {winner}. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL beats its effort frontmatter, which beats --effort and the settings that count for its own model.

quotes.quote: Effort level when this subagent is active. Overrides the session effort level, but not the `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` environment variable.

rules.reason: {agent} is set to {value} in {file} but runs as {becomes}, because maxEffortLevel caps {model} at {becomes}.

quotes.quote: Any higher level runs at the cap instead, including one from `/effort`, the `/model` picker, `--effort`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, a skill's or subagent's `effort` frontmatter, or the model's own default.

rules.reason: {agent} runs on {model}, which has no {value} level, so {value} from {file} runs as {becomes}.

quotes.quote: If you set a level the active model does not support, Claude Code falls back to the highest supported level at or below the one you set. For example, `xhigh` runs as `high` on Opus 4.6.

rules.reason: The entry in {file} matches {model} by canonical name, alias, date suffix, [1m] or a provider-style ID. In one file, a canonical-name entry beats an alias entry.

quotes.quote: Claude Code writes each entry under the model's canonical name, such as `claude-opus-5-5`, and matches that model's alias, date-suffixed, `[1m]`, and recognized provider-specific IDs to the same entry.

rules.reason: {file} caps {model} at {value}, replacing that file's top-level maxEffortLevel for this model only. Across files, the lowest cap still applies.

quotes.quote: That entry replaces this key for the model only within the settings source that sets both, such as your user settings or one managed source.

rules.reason: {file} sets the auto-compact window for {model}, and in that file the per-model value beats the top-level autoCompactWindow.

quotes.quote: For that model, the value takes precedence over a top-level `autoCompactWindow` in the same settings file. Requires Claude Code v2.1.288 or later
